content.jointProblem: Can Serbian morphological normalization combined with script-aware retrieval reduce LinguaBot's useful-result miss rate toward its below-5% target while supporting vocabulary updates without full re-indexing? The first experiment would compare the current Elasticsearch baseline against normalization-order and query-expansion variants on held-out support queries, separately testing inflections, within-word script mixing, and new product terms, while measuring retrieval quality, latency, and update effort.

rationale.text: His research directly examines the interaction between Serbian morphological reduction and script normalization, providing a relevant basis for testing pipeline ordering rather than treating the two problems independently.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.

rationale.text: He has evaluated phoneme-based canonicalization for Serbian retrieval on annotated relevance pairs, making this a grounded candidate for addressing cross-script mismatches.

sources.quote: We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

rationale.text: His work on transliteration-based query expansion offers a query-side alternative worth testing where changes to indexed representations would be costly.

sources.quote: This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index.

rationale.text: He has studied incremental indexing with script normalization, which is relevant to designing updates, although it does not establish that changing vocabulary rules can avoid re-indexing existing content.

sources.quote: Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja.

rationale.text: His group has experience integrating a normalization module into existing enterprise search systems rather than replacing the entire application.

sources.quote: Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema.

constraints.text: The prototype must address Serbian inflection and automatic script-mixing tolerance in the existing Elasticsearch environment, including within-word mixing rather than only whole-token transliteration.

sources.quote: our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.
Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.

constraints.text: Vocabulary maintenance must avoid a full re-index and remain manageable; simply replacing the current manually maintained synonym lists would not meet the task.

sources.quote: maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.

constraints.text: Evaluation should use the company's labelled support data and linguistic validation, with the below-5% miss rate treated as an acceptance target to test, not a demonstrated outcome.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.

constraints.text: Scope must fit approximately EUR 8,000 for tooling or data work and deliver something testable within six months; this is not evidence of a separate research-services budget.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: The engagement must remain a small, research-focused contract or consultancy: the researcher reports two active projects and capacity for only one smaller industrial engagement.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Results on legal, news, web, and encyclopedia material may not transfer to short banking and telecom support queries. The first experiment must explicitly test this domain shift, within-word script mixing, and unseen terminology.

Morphology and script errors account for more than half of the observed misses, not necessarily enough to reach below 5% by fixing those errors alone; missing content or ranking failures may impose a remaining floor.
Published enterprise pilots still required terminology updates, and incremental ingestion does not prove that changed normalization rules can update existing indexed terms without re-indexing.
Foreign names, abbreviations, and alphanumeric product terms are documented transliteration exceptions; normalization may merge distinct terms or damage exact-match retrieval.

Joint-project willingness is open, but the researcher's start date and committed hours remain unknown. Company hardware, latency limits, data-sharing permissions, and funding for researcher time are also unspecified.
questions: What start date, hours, and deliverables can the researcher commit to within the six-month window, and how will research services be funded alongside the EUR 8,000 tooling/data budget?
Can the researcher access de-identified queries, relevance labels, and corresponding knowledge-base snapshots, and what client permissions, retention rules, and deployment restrictions apply?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth, and can the 12,000-query bank baseline be reproduced with consistent labels and a time-held-out evaluation set?

Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers, and extension mechanisms are available, and what exactly counts as a prohibited full re-index? Are query-side expansion, partial updates, or auxiliary dictionaries acceptable?
What latency, throughput, memory, and hardware limits must the prototype meet, and can external APIs or neural components be used?
Can the two linguists validate stratified error sets and newly introduced terminology, and who will own ongoing updates, regression tests, and maintenance after the project?
